vessels.name: Allianz Juno
vessels.$comment: Replaced by Charlie 3, whose first report is 20 May 2026; Juno's last is 16 May. Without retired_on the app would carry Juno's final position forward for ever and draw it alongside Charlie 3 at the same berth, showing two vessels where there is one.

vessels.name: Charlie 3
vessels.$comment: Charlie 3 took over Allianz Juno's role and berth on 20 May 2026, the date of its first report; Juno is retired on that date (see JUNO.retired_on) so only one of the two is ever on the map. Berth B4 is confirmed by its own logs ('VSL STBY ALS TO B# 4 IN SHUAIBA PORT'). IDENTITY CONFIRMED 2026-07-29 against public trackers: MyShipTracking lists MMSI 341930000 as 'High speed craft', 42 x 7 m, call sign V4DX4, flag St Kitts & Nevis, with 144 arrivals at Shuaiba in the past year on a Shuaiba<->Dubai pattern, and its last recorded position (29.04054, 48.15859) is 12 m from our own Berth 4 coordinates — i.e. the same mooring. That settles the earlier worry that this was the wrong hull: VesselFinder's 'Offshore Tug/Supply' label is just a coarser classification of the same ship. Length and beam above are now those real 42 x 7 m figures, replacing Juno's 48 x 11 m stand-in; speed_kts 14 is still Juno's number and remains unverified, which is why specs_provisional stays true. Its fuel tank is 55 m3 against Juno's 147 m3, consistent with the smaller hull. The .env AIS_MMSI_CH3 entry is what the pollers actually read; these fields are documentation.
